newsitem.title: USA: PECO proposes retail wheeling pilot.
newsitem.headline: PECO proposes retail wheeling pilot.

text.p: PECO Energy Co filed Thursday with the Pennsylvania Public Utility Commission a pilot program to enable some 90,000 residential, commercial and industrial customers to choose their electric suppliers beginning as early as October, the utility said.
PECO said it believes this will be the largest electric pilot program in the country.
If it is approved, the company said, the pilot would begin in April with the random selection by a neutral third party of some 90,000 customers from the PECO Energy service territory.

Under the pilot, PECO said, the 90,000 customers will have the opportunity to buy their electricity from other power companies, brokers or marketers through 1998. Cumulatively, about 480 megawatts of power will be open to competition.

The power from other suppliers would continue to be delivered over PECO transmission and distribution lines, and the utility would continue to supply customer services such as meter reading, billing and outage restoration, it noted.
The cross section of eligible PECO Energy customers will include 5 percent from the City of Philadelphia and 5 percent from suburban counties across all major rate classes.
Also, residential customers in one randomly selected township or borough in the suburbs and one randomly selected political subdivision in the City will be eligible.
In addition, randomly selected commercial and industrial customers located in state-created Enterprise Zones also will be eligible, PECO said.

The filing is in compliance with Pennsylvania's recent electric competition legislation, which provided for customer choice pilot programs for about 5 percent of the peak load of the state's electric utilities, beginning in 1997.

The pilots will be the first step in the Commonwealth's transition to full electric competition, under which one-third of a utility's customers will be able to choose their electric suppliers by 1999, another third by 2000 and the final third by 2001.
All pilot participants would be among the one-third of electric utility customers to be offered choice by January 1, 1999, PECO said. ((-- Jim Brumm 212-859-1710.))
